questions.question_text: Utah recognizes which types of brokerage agency relationships?
distractors: Seller and buyer agency only
Seller, buyer, designated, and transaction
Single agency and dual agency only
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401a recognizes seller agency, buyer agency, and limited agency — representing both parties in one transaction with prior informed consent. Utah has no transaction-broker, facilitator, or designated-agency status; a limited agent acts as a neutral third party.

questions.question_text: A broker represents both the buyer and seller in the same transaction with the informed consent of both parties. This relationship is called:
distractors: Designated agency
Transaction brokerage
Facilitator relationship
questions.explanation: Representing both parties in Utah is limited agency. 61-2f-401(2) requires informed written consent from both, and R162-2f-401a(4) requires the limited agent to act as a neutral third party who cannot advocate for either side.

questions.question_text: A listing agent's buyer client wants to purchase one of the agent's own listings. Before proceeding, the agent must:
questions.correct_answer: Obtain informed consent for limited agency
distractors: Refer the buyer to another brokerage
Cancel the listing agreement first
Notify the Division of Real Estate
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401a(3) requires prior informed consent in writing: the licensee must explain what will be kept confidential and what will be disclosed, and obtain each party's written acknowledgment that they waive undivided loyalty, absolute confidentiality, and full disclosure. Acting for both without that consent violates 61-2f-401(2).

questions.question_text: In a limited agency arrangement, the broker's role changes because they:
questions.correct_answer: Cannot advocate for either party over the other
distractors: No longer owe any duties to either party
Must favor the party who listed first
Can only communicate through attorneys
questions.explanation: A Utah limited agent is a neutral third party (R162-2f-401a(4)). Only four duties survive to both sides: obedience consistent with neutrality, reasonable care and diligence, safekeeping of money and property, and any duties the agency agreement adds. Loyalty, absolute confidentiality, and full disclosure are expressly waived.

questions.question_text: A seller tells their agent their minimum acceptable price is $400,000 but lists at $450,000. If the agent enters limited agency, this pricing information is:
distractors: Required to be disclosed to the buyer
Only confidential for 30 days
Shared at the broker's discretion
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401b(1)(t) bars a limited agent from disclosing information given by either principal that would likely weaken that party's bargaining position, unless that principal permits it. The seller's walk-away price is exactly that kind of information, so it stays confidential.

questions.question_text: Which duty does a Utah agent owe to ALL parties in a transaction, not just their client?
distractors: Loyalty and obedience to instructions
Confidentiality of financial details
Reasonable care and due diligence
questions.explanation: 61-2f-401(1) bars misrepresentation to anyone, and R162-2f-401a(6) requires written disclosure of the licensee's agency relationships and of any principal interest to clients, other agents, and unrepresented parties. Even the client-confidentiality duty does not cover a known property defect or a client's inability to perform (R162-2f-401a(1)(d)).

questions.question_text: A buyer's agent discovers that the property has foundation issues not yet disclosed. The agent must:
questions.correct_answer: Disclose this material fact to their client
distractors: Wait for the seller to disclose it first
Only disclose if the client specifically asks
Keep it confidential as the seller's agent shared it
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401a(1)(c) requires full disclosure to the principal of any material fact the agent learns about the property, the other party, or the transaction. Foundation problems plainly qualify.

questions.question_text: Under Utah rules, by when must a licensee disclose agency relationships in writing?
questions.correct_answer: Before the parties execute a binding purchase or lease agreement
distractors: Only at the closing appointment
Within 48 hours of first contact
Only if a party asks about representation
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401a(6)(c) requires written disclosure of agency relationships to clients, other agents, and unrepresented parties before a binding purchase or lease agreement is executed, and R162-2f-401a(10) requires that prior disclosure to be confirmed in the REPC. The relationship must also be disclosed to another agent on initial contact (401a(9)).

questions.question_text: A seller's agent learns the buyer cannot qualify for financing. The agent's duty regarding this information is to:
questions.correct_answer: Disclose it to their seller client
distractors: Keep it confidential from all parties
Only share it if asked directly
Report it to the Division immediately
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401a(1)(c) obligates the agent to inform the principal of any material fact learned about the other party. A buyer's inability to obtain financing goes directly to performance, so the seller must be told.

questions.question_text: Which set of duties does a Utah agent owe specifically to their client?
distractors: Honesty and fair dealing to all parties
Disclosure of known material facts only
Fair treatment and equal service to all
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401a(1) lists the duties owed to a principal: loyalty, obedience, full disclosure, confidentiality, reasonable care and diligence, safekeeping and accounting, plus any duties the agency agreement adds.

questions.question_text: An exclusive buyer representation agreement gives which right to the broker?
questions.correct_answer: The exclusive right to represent the buyer
distractors: The right to set the purchase price
Automatic commission from any seller
Authority to sign contracts for the buyer
questions.explanation: 61-2f-308(1)(d) defines an exclusive brokerage agreement as one giving the principal broker the sole right to act as the client's agent. It also obligates that broker to accept and present offers and to help the client develop and respond to them (61-2f-308(2)).

questions.question_text: Which element must be clearly stated in a Utah exclusive brokerage agreement?
distractors: The minimum sale price of properties
The number of properties to be shown
The agent's personal contact information
questions.explanation: Two Utah rules converge here: R162-2f-401a(2) requires a written agency agreement defining the scope of the relationship, and 25-5-4(1)(e) makes any agreement employing a broker to buy or sell real estate for compensation void unless it is in writing and signed.

questions.question_text: A seller's principal broker gives blank forms to an unrepresented buyer and negotiates terms directly with them. Under Utah law this conduct:
questions.correct_answer: Does not by itself create an agency relationship with the buyer
distractors: Automatically makes the broker a limited agent
Creates buyer agency by implication
Is prohibited unless the buyer signs a waiver
questions.explanation: 61-2f-308(5), added by H.B. 419 in 2025, provides that a seller's principal broker who contacts an unrepresented buyer, provides blank forms, or negotiates terms does not thereby create an agency relationship with that buyer.

questions.question_text: A buyer signed an exclusive agreement with Broker A but then works with Broker B to purchase a home. The buyer may owe:
questions.correct_answer: Compensation to Broker A per the agreement
distractors: Nothing, as the buyer can work with anyone
Compensation to both brokers equally
A penalty fee to the Division
questions.explanation: Under 61-2f-308(1)(d) an exclusive brokerage agreement gives one principal broker the sole right to represent the client, so buying through another broker during its term can still leave the buyer owing compensation under the agreement's terms.

questions.question_text: A seller wants to list with two different brokerages simultaneously. This is:
questions.correct_answer: Not possible under an exclusive agreement
distractors: Standard practice in Utah
Required for properties over $500,000
Only allowed with Division approval
questions.explanation: An exclusive listing gives one principal broker the sole right to represent the seller, and R162-2f-401b(1)(k) bars a licensee from entering a concurrent agency representation when the licensee knows the principal already has an agreement with another licensee.
